'''Dominique Pierre Perrin'''<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.letudiant.fr/educpros/personnalites/perrin-dominique-pierre-739.html|title = Dominique PERRIN: Biographie et actualités sur EducPros}}</ref> (b. 1946) is a French [[mathematician]] and [[Theoretical computer science|theoretical computer scientist]] known for his contributions to [[coding theory]] and to [[combinatorics on words]]. He is a professor of the [[University of Marne-la-Vallée]] and currently serves as the President of [[ESIEE Paris]].

==Biography==

Perrin earned his PhD from [[Paris Diderot University|Paris 7 University]] in 1975. In his early career, he was a [[CNRS]] researcher (1970–1977) and taught at the [[University of Chile]] (1972–1973). Later, he worked as a professor at the [[University of Rouen]] (1977–1983), [[Paris Diderot University|Paris 7 University]] (1983–1993), and [[École Polytechnique]] (1982–2002). Since 1993, Perrin is a professor at the [[University of Marne-la-Vallée]], and since 2004, he is the President of [[ESIEE Paris]].

Perrin is a member of [[Academia Europaea]] since 1989.

==Scientific contributions==

Perrin has been a member of the [[M. Lothaire|Lothaire]] group of mathematicians that developed the foundations of combinatorics on words. He has co-authored three scientific monographs: "Theory of Codes" (1985),<ref>{{cite book | last1=Berstel | first1=Jean | last2=Perrin | first2=Dominique | author1-link = Jean Berstel | title=Theory of Codes | publisher=Academic Press | series=Pure and Applied Mathematics | isbn=978-0-120-93420-1 | year=1985 | volume=117}}</ref> "Codes and Automata" (2009),<ref>{{cite book | last1=Berstel | first1=Jean | last2=Perrin | first2=Dominique | last3=Reutenauer | first3=Christophe | author1-link = Jean Berstel | title=Codes and Automata | publisher=Cambridge University Press | series=Encyclopedia of Mathematics and its Applications | isbn=978-0-521-88831-8 | year=2009 | volume=129}}</ref> and "Infinite Words" (2004),<ref>{{cite book | last1=Perrin | first1=Dominique | last2=Pin | first2=Jean-Éric | title=Infinite Words: Automata, Semigroups, Logic and Games | publisher=Academic Press | series=Pure and Applied Mathematics | isbn=978-0-125-32111-2 | year=2004 | volume=141}}</ref> as well as the three [[M. Lothaire|Lothaire books]].<ref>{{cite book | last1=Lothaire | first1=M. | editor=<!-- none, bad meta-data--> | title=Combinatorics on Words | doi=10.1017/CBO9780511566097 | publisher=Addison-Wesley Publishing Co., Reading, Mass. | series=Encyclopedia of Mathematics and its Applications | isbn=978-0-201-13516-9 | mr=675953 | year=1983 | volume=17 | url-access=registration | url=https://archive.org/details/combinatoricsonw0000loth }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | last1=Lothaire | first1=M. | title=Algebraic Combinatorics on Words | url=https://archive.org/details/algebraiccombina0000loth | publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] | series=Encyclopedia of Mathematics and its Applications | isbn=978-0-521-81220-7 | mr=1905123 | year=2002 | volume=90 | doi=10.1017/CBO9781107326019 | url-access=registration }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | last1=Lothaire | first1=M. | title=Applied Combinatorics on Words | url=https://archive.org/details/appliedcombinato0000loth | publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] | series=Encyclopedia of Mathematics and its Applications | isbn=978-0-521-84802-2 | mr=2165687 | year=2005 | volume=105 | doi=10.1017/CBO9781107341005 | url-access=registration }}</ref>
Perrin has published around 50 research articles in [[formal language theory]].
